samples.summary: MemDocStore's documented throw-with-writes behaviour (checkpoint kept so the partial mess is undoable) has no test
samples.evidence: `MemDocStore.batch()` (src/store/memory.ts:228-236) explicitly documents "On a throw the partial writes stand ... so the checkpoint is kept — that is what makes the mess undoable." The only throwing test added, 're-arms snapshotting after the batch ends, even on a throw', throws from a body that made NO writes, so it exercises the `wroteNothing` pop branch, not the keep branch. Nothing asserts that after `batch(() => { store.insertText(...); throw })` the store `canUndo()` and `undo()` restores the pre-batch document. If the `wroteNothing` comparison ever mis-fires (e.g. clone normalization drift), the partial writes become permanently unundoable and no test fails.
searchedFor: read full batch() describe block in packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts

samples.summary: Nested-batch test for MemDocStore never asserts the nested body's write actually landed
samples.evidence: 'a nested batch does not add a second undo unit' writes '!' then, in a nested batch, '?', then immediately undoes and asserts 'Hello' / `canUndo() === false`. It never asserts the document was 'Hello!?' before the undo, so the test passes identically if the nested batch dropped or discarded the inner write. The Yorkie sibling test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, 'a nested batch does not open a second undo unit') explicitly adds that assertion and explains why it is needed; the memory-store test omits it.

samples.summary: `Doc.batch` happy-path test asserts nothing that distinguishes batching from a plain call
samples.evidence: 'runs the body through the store batch' only asserts that `insertText` inside the callback produced 'hello'. That holds whether `Doc.batch` delegates to `store.batch`, or simply invokes `fn()` — no spy on `store.batch`, no undo-unit count (e.g. `store.canUndo()` after two snapshots), nothing. The test name claims routing through the store seam but the assertion cannot observe it.

samples.summary: Failed-redefinition cache test relies on a negative `not.toBe(33)` assertion that can pass for unrelated reasons
samples.evidence: 'a failed redefinition leaves the editor matching the store' ends with `expect(editor.getRangeStyleSummary().fontSize).not.toBe(33)`. A negative assertion passes if the summary returns `undefined`, `'mixed'`, a default, or if the selection change silently failed — none of which prove the cached document was refreshed from the store. A positive assertion (e.g. comparing against the store's resolved value, or asserting `doc`'s cached styles no longer contain the rolled-back heading-6 definition) would pin the behaviour the test is named for.

samples.summary: No test covers the new `finally { invalidateLayout(); render(); }` / `notifyStyleApplied` placement in withNamedStyleChange
samples.evidence: The change deliberately moved repaint into a `finally` (so a failed pass repaints from what the store really holds) and left `notifyStyleApplied()` after it on the success path only. The only failing-path test ('a failed redefinition leaves the editor matching the store') asserts store/cache state, never that a repaint happened after the throw nor that the style-applied notification was suppressed. If either were reordered back, no test fails, and the visible symptom is a stale canvas after a failed style redefinition.
searchedFor: grep for notifyStyleApplied/onCursorMove assertions in frontend docs tests

samples.summary: `setDocStyles` — one of the four entry points rewired through withNamedStyleChange — has no test at all
samples.evidence: The new frontend suite covers `updateStyleToMatch`, `resetNamedStyle` and `resetAllNamedStyles`, but grepping the repo for `setDocStyles` finds it only in editor.ts, document.ts, frontend UI components and this same frontend test file (where it is never called). So the 'use my default styles' path now runs inside a batch with no coverage of its undo cost or its sweep, in either package.

samples.summary: The batch presence-skip is tested only for the published presence, not for the local anchors it deliberately keeps running
samples.evidence: `updateCursorPos` now returns early via `skipNonHistoryPresence()` *after* setting `localSelectionAnchor` / cursor anchors, with a comment asserting 'the anchors above are view-local bookkeeping and always run'. The added tests ('holds back a non-history presence write inside a batch', 'restores the pre-edit caret...') only assert `getPresenceCursorPos()`; nothing asserts the anchors were still updated inside a batch, so moving the guard above the anchor code would go undetected. The second skip site (the `publishResolvedPresence`-style path near line 1242) has no batch test at all.
searchedFor: read skipNonHistoryPresence and both call sites in yorkie-doc-store.ts

samples.summary: No test that a batch which DOES write clears the redo stack
samples.evidence: `MemDocStore.batch()` clears `redoStack` up front and restores `priorRedo` only when the batch wrote nothing. Two tests pin the restore branch ('a batch that writes nothing leaves redo history intact', 'a self-reverting batch leaves redo history intact'); none pin the complementary case — after an undo, a batch that writes must leave `canRedo() === false`. If the restore condition inverted, a redo would resurrect a document from a diverged history and the tests would stay green.
searchedFor: read batch() describe block in packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts

samples.summary: New `describe('batch')` block is nested inside the unrelated `describe('image inlines')` suite
samples.evidence: The added block is appended before the closing brace of `describe('image inlines', ...)` (the file's last top-level describe), so batch tests report under 'image inlines > batch'. Cosmetic, but it makes the suite name misleading when a batch test fails.
